# Cross-platform desktop release (Linux, Windows, macOS) for formal-ai.
#
# Produces the exact assets the /download page (js/download) resolves from
# the GitHub Releases API:
#   formal-ai-desktop-macos-<arch>-<version>.{dmg,zip}
#   formal-ai-desktop-windows-installer-<arch>-<version>.exe
#   formal-ai-desktop-windows-portable-<arch>-<version>.exe
#   formal-ai-desktop-linux-<arch>-<version>.{AppImage,deb,tar.gz}
#   latest.yml, latest-mac.yml, latest-linux.yml, and *.blockmap updater metadata
#   (Electron Builder emits x86_64/amd64 Linux x64 aliases; the build job
#    normalizes them to x64 before checksums/uploads and rewrites update metadata.)
# plus a consolidated SHA256SUMS.txt and BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt, and SLSA build
# provenance attestations (verifiable with `gh attestation verify`).
#
# Triggers:
#   * release: published     - fires for releases published manually (UI) or via
#                              a PAT. NOTE: the automated `[Rust] x.y.z` releases
#                              created by the CI/CD Pipeline use GITHUB_TOKEN, so
#                              GitHub suppresses the `release` event for them
#                              (recursion guard). The workflow_run trigger below
#                              covers that case automatically.
#   * workflow_run           - after the "CI/CD Pipeline" completes on main (with
#                              ANY conclusion except cancelled/skipped -- the
#                              release is published in an early job, so a later job
#                              failing must not suppress the desktop build), build
#                              desktop assets for the resolved release tag
#                              (idempotent: skips when assets already exist).
#   * workflow_dispatch      - manual rebuild for a specific (or latest) tag.
name: Desktop Release

# zizmor flags every `workflow_run` trigger as fundamentally insecure, because the
# usual shape of one -- re-running a pull request's own head in a context that has
# write permissions and secrets -- is arbitrary code execution by any fork. This
# workflow is not that shape, on two independent counts:
#
#   1. The `resolve` job refuses any `workflow_run` whose `head_branch` is not
#      `main` (see its `if:` below), so a fork's pipeline run cannot reach it.
#   2. Nothing downstream ever checks out `workflow_run.head_sha`. The privileged
#      jobs check out `needs.resolve.outputs.tag` -- a release tag that
#      scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh reads back from this repository's own
#      Releases API. Untrusted code is never the build input, so even if a fork
#      branch named `main` slipped past (1), the worst case is a redundant build
#      of an already-published tag, which the idempotency guard then skips.
#
# Issue #1076: recorded rather than silenced, so the next person to add a
# `workflow_run` consumer has to re-establish both counts.
on: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Release tag to build (e.g. v0.152.0). Leave blank for the latest release."
        required: false
        default: ""
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI/CD Pipeline"]
    types: [completed]
    # Issue #1081 (D8): without this filter the event fires for EVERY pipeline
    # completion, including the pull_request runs of every feature branch. The
    # `resolve` job below then rejects them on `head_branch == 'main'`, so the
    # whole run concludes `skipped`. Measured over 2026-08-31..2026-09-07: 107
    # workflow_run-triggered runs, 102 of them skipped (95.3%), and 99 of those
    # 102 correlate 1:1 with a pull-request pipeline finishing on a feature
    # branch (dev/log/issues/1081/pulls/1082/measurements/desktop-release-workflow-run-noise.md).
    # Every run that did real work was triggered by a `push` pipeline on main.
    # `branches` on workflow_run matches the TRIGGERING workflow's branch --
    # "You can use the `branches` or `branches-ignore` filter to specify what
    # branches the triggering workflow must run on in order to trigger your
    # workflow" -- so this drops exactly the noise and keeps all five useful
    # runs. The `head_branch == 'main'` guard in `resolve` stays: it is one of
    # the two counts that make this `workflow_run` trigger safe (see the header
    # comment), and a trigger filter is not a substitute for that argument.
    branches: [main]
  # Issue #808: packaging and macOS signing used to run only after a release
  # existed, so a desktop regression was always discovered post-merge -- which is
  # exactly how the "unsealed contents present in the root directory of an
  # embedded framework" codesign failure reached main. On pull requests the same
  # build matrix runs in dry-run mode: everything up to and including the smoke
  # tests, with every publishing step (attest, release upload, SHA256SUMS)
  # skipped. Path-filtered so unrelated pull requests do not pay for six runners.
  pull_request:
    # Issue #1187 R4: an isolated e2e/<purpose>/<run>/<name> pull request
    # never triggers this repository's own pipeline.
    branches-ignore: ['e2e/**']
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - 'desktop/**'
      - 'vscode/**'
      - '.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml'
      - 'scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh'
      - 'scripts/install-node-dependencies.sh'
      # The build job runs `cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --release --bin formal-ai` and bundles
      # the result, so a Rust-only change can break desktop packaging while
      # touching none of the paths above. Without these entries that breakage is
      # a false negative on the pull request and only surfaces post-merge --
      # precisely the failure mode issue #808 was filed for.
      - 'rust/src/**'
      - 'rust/Cargo.toml'
      - 'rust/Cargo.lock'

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
  CARGO_NET_RETRY: '10'
  CARGO_HTTP_MULTIPLEXING: 'false'
  RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings

jobs:
  resolve:
    name: Resolve target release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-resolve
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # For workflow_run, continue after ANY completed main-branch pipeline except
    # cancelled/skipped runs (issue #479). We intentionally do NOT gate on
    # conclusion == 'success': the auto-release publishes the GitHub release in an
    # EARLY pipeline job, so a LATER job failing (e.g. the E2E Pages probe timing
    # out) still leaves a real, asset-less release that desktop assets must heal.
    # Gating on full-pipeline green meant one unrelated late failure suppressed
    # every desktop build -> "Not available in latest release". The actual
    # decision to build is delegated to scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh, whose
    # idempotency guard skips when the resolved release already carries desktop
    # assets, so running on a non-success conclusion is safe and self-healing.
    # Pull requests resolve nothing: there is no release to heal and no tag to
    # check out. The job is skipped and `build` admits the skipped dependency
    # explicitly, so the packaging matrix still runs against the PR head.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' &&
      (github.event_name != 'workflow_run' ||
      (github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'skipped'))
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.tag }}
      should_build: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.should_build }}
    steps:
      # Check out the repo so the resolve logic lives in a unit-tested script
      # (scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh) instead of being inlined here. The
      # script only needs to *exist*; it queries the GitHub API for everything
      # else, so checking out the default ref is sufficient.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve tag and whether desktop assets are needed
        id: pick
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          INPUT_TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          WORKFLOW_RUN_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        # Issue #479: the automated release tags a CHILD "chore: release vX.Y.Z"
        # commit whose first parent is the completed CI head SHA, so matching the
        # tag to the head SHA directly always failed and desktop assets were
        # never built. desktop-release-resolve.sh resolves the latest release
        # instead (with a defensive exact-SHA tier and an idempotency guard) and
        # emits verbose ::group:: diagnostics for future debugging.
        run: bash scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh

  # Issue #1017 (D19): the six packaging legs of run 31993872684 started across
  # 62 minutes, and each resolved the base branch tip itself -- `linux-x64` and
  # `macos-arm64` merged 1858b3386 while `windows-arm64` merged d1439e557, so
  # six installers built from two source trees shipped as one release set with
  # nothing comparing them. One commit for every merge in this run.
  base:
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-base
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/pin-base-commit.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.label }}
    needs: [resolve, base]
    concurrency:
      group: desktop-release-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}-${{ matrix.label }}
      queue: max
    # `resolve` is skipped on pull requests, and a skipped dependency would
    # normally skip this job too -- hence the explicit `!cancelled()`.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || needs.resolve.outputs.should_build == 'true') }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,    ebflag: "--linux", label: "linux-x64",     binext: "",     capmin: 40 }
          - { os: ubuntu-24.04-arm, ebflag: "--linux", label: "linux-arm64",   binext: "",     capmin: 40 }
          - { os: macos-15-intel,   ebflag: "--mac",   label: "macos-x64",     binext: "",     capmin: 50 }
          - { os: macos-14,         ebflag: "--mac",   label: "macos-arm64",   binext: "",     capmin: 40 }
          - { os: windows-latest,   ebflag: "--win",   label: "windows-x64",   binext: ".exe", capmin: 50 }
          - { os: windows-11-arm,   ebflag: "--win",   label: "windows-arm64", binext: ".exe", capmin: 50 }
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Windows ARM64 normally takes 25-28 minutes, and runs 30573608801
    # (attempts 1 and 2) were both cancelled at the former 30-minute cap while
    # electron-builder was completing a valid installer. Keep the job bounded
    # while allowing for runner and antivirus/file-lock variance.
    #
    # Issue #896 added the published web-search/web-capture Rust crates. Their
    # current releases expose the server/browser dependency graphs
    # unconditionally (upstream web-search#22 and web-capture#148). On the cold
    # macos-15-intel runner in run 30788311906, release compilation took 33m21s
    # and the otherwise-valid job hit the 40-minute cap while creating the DMG.
    # The Windows targets moved the same way: in run 30832897812, windows-x64
    # compiled for 17m39s, packaged a valid installer, and was cancelled at the
    # cap while uploading its checksum fragment, with windows-arm64 finishing at
    # 36m04s. Give those three targets bounded packaging headroom until the
    # adapter-only upstream features let us remove the heavyweight graph; the
    # Linux and macOS ARM64 targets stay well under 40 minutes.
    #
    # The cap lives in the matrix (`capmin`) rather than in an expression here
    # so that the packaging retry guard can be derived from the *same* number:
    # two independent copies of "50" would drift, and a guard computed from a
    # stale cap is worse than no guard at all.
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.capmin }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Issue #1017: the packaging retry must know how much of the job clock is
      # left, not how long packaging usually takes. `timeout-minutes` starts
      # before this step, so the reserve covers both the runner's own set-up and
      # everything that has to happen *after* packaging (artifact normalization,
      # the DMG mount/codesign smoke test, checksums and uploads).
      - name: Record the job deadline
        env:
          JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: ${{ matrix.capmin }}
          POST_PACKAGING_RESERVE_SECONDS: "360"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES * 60 - POST_PACKAGING_RESERVE_SECONDS ))
          echo "FORMAL_AI_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH=${deadline}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # On pull requests there is no resolved tag: build the PR head, which
          # is the whole point of the dry run.
          ref: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.resolve.outputs.tag || '' }}
          # Quoted '0'/'1': GitHub's `&&`/`||` treat the number 0 as falsy, so an
          # unquoted 0 here would silently select the other branch.
          # 0 is needed by simulate-fresh-merge.sh, which merges origin/<base>.
          fetch-depth: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '0' || '1' }}

      # Issue #812: `release.yml` simulates the fresh merge in `lint` and `test`,
      # but this workflow -- the only one that packages the desktop app -- did
      # not, so the packaging dry run validated the PR head against a merge
      # preview that predates any commit pushed to the base branch since the last
      # sync. A packaging break introduced by a concurrent main commit stayed
      # invisible until after the merge, which is how desktop breakages have
      # reached tags before.
      - name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          # Issue #1017: the commit resolved once by `base`, so all six
          # packaging legs merge the same one however far apart they start.
          BASE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.base.outputs.commit }}
        run: bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Cache Rust compiler outputs
        # Cargo can use a response file for web-sys's generated feature-check
        # arguments on Windows, but sccache respawns rustc with the expanded
        # command and hits CreateProcess's command-line limit (os error 206).
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        uses: mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.11
        with:
          # v0.17.0 expands Rust response files before spawning rustc and
          # exceeds the Windows command-line limit for web-sys.
          version: v0.16.0

      - name: Enable Rust compiler cache
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          echo "SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Keep Cargo's dependency cache out of this matrix. A cold Windows build
      # completes inside the job budget, while actions/cache registers a
      # post-job archive of Cargo home: on run 30398883119 all product work and
      # uploads passed, then compressing 194 MB consumed the remaining 3m40 and
      # GitHub cancelled the otherwise-successful job. Unix runners retain
      # expensive compiler outputs through sccache without that post-packaging
      # failure mode; Windows uses Cargo's direct rustc response-file path.
      - name: Build formal-ai binary (release)
        run: cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --release --bin formal-ai

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Install desktop dependencies
        run: scripts/install-node-dependencies.sh desktop

      # Issue #990: execute the real published command-stream adapter after the
      # production dependency tree is installed, on every packaged platform.
      - name: Test command-stream production adapter
        working-directory: desktop
        run: node --test scripts/command-runner.test.mjs

      - name: Prepare desktop resources (web + bundled binary + version sync)
        working-directory: desktop
        run: node scripts/prepare-resources.mjs

      # Issue #1017: electron-builder fetches its 7-Zip toolset -- and, on
      # macOS, the dmgbuild bundle -- with a single `got` request whose only
      # deadline is 600 000 ms. In run 95255998673 that request stalled for the
      # full ten minutes on macos-15-intel: the retry underneath recovered, the
      # DMG, ZIP and both blockmaps were written, and the build still failed
      # because AsyncTaskManager.awaitTasks() rethrew the timeout it had already
      # recorded. Seeding the checksum-validated archive cache that
      # `downloadAndExtract` consults before it touches the network removes the
      # request itself. Every failure here is a warning only, so packaging falls
      # back to downloading the toolset exactly as it does today.
      - name: Prefetch electron-builder toolsets
        working-directory: desktop
        run: node scripts/prefetch-builder-toolsets.mjs

      - name: Check macOS signing secrets
        if: matrix.ebflag == '--mac'
        id: mac_secrets
        env:
          MAC_CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.MAC_CSC_LINK }}
          MAC_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MAC_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_API_KEY }}
          APPLE_API_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_API_KEY_ID }}
          APPLE_API_ISSUER: ${{ secrets.APPLE_API_ISSUER }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=()
          for name in MAC_CSC_LINK MAC_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD APPLE_API_KEY APPLE_API_KEY_ID APPLE_API_ISSUER; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then
              missing+=("$name")
            fi
          done

          if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "has_secrets=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "mode=adhoc" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::macOS signing/notarization secrets are not configured: ${missing[*]}"
            echo "Building ad-hoc signed macOS artifacts without notarization for direct testing."
          else
            echo "has_secrets=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "mode=signed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      # Issue #1055: through the retry wrapper, like the macOS legs. The
      # toolset download electron-builder makes is the same on every platform,
      # and `Build windows-x64` failed on `read ECONNRESET` mid-download while
      # the previous run of that job, on the same branch, had succeeded.
      - name: Package desktop app (Linux/Windows)
        if: matrix.ebflag != '--mac'
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
          # Issue #1017's rule applies here too: without the deadline a retry
          # can outlive the job clock, and GitHub reports that kill as
          # `cancelled` rather than `failure`.
          FORMAL_AI_MACOS_PACKAGE_DEADLINE_EPOCH: ${{ env.FORMAL_AI_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH }}
        run: bash scripts/package-macos-with-retry.sh ${{ matrix.ebflag }} --publish never

      - name: Package desktop app (macOS signed)
        if: matrix.ebflag == '--mac' && steps.mac_secrets.outputs.has_secrets == 'true'
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.MAC_CSC_LINK }}
          CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MAC_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_API_KEY }}
          APPLE_API_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_API_KEY_ID }}
          APPLE_API_ISSUER: ${{ secrets.APPLE_API_ISSUER }}
          DEBUG: electron-builder,electron-notarize*
          # The retry wrapper refuses an attempt the job cannot finish. See the
          # comment on the ad-hoc step below.
          FORMAL_AI_MACOS_PACKAGE_DEADLINE_EPOCH: ${{ env.FORMAL_AI_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH }}
        run: bash scripts/package-macos-with-retry.sh ${{ matrix.ebflag }} --publish never

      # Issue #479: electron-builder 26 changed macOS signing control flow. Its
      # MacPackager.sign() now calls findSigningIdentity(), which returns null --
      # skipping signing entirely and NEVER invoking the custom `mac.sign` hook --
      # unless a real identity is found OR `mac.identity` is exactly "-" (ad-hoc).
      # See packages/app-builder-lib/src/targets/mac/MacTargetHelper.ts: only the
      # `qualifier === "-"` branch yields an Identity when no certificate exists.
      # Without `-c.mac.identity=-` the produced .app had no _CodeSignature, so the
      # pre-upload smoke test failed with "missing its signed CodeResources
      # envelope" and macOS assets were never published. Passing identity="-" makes
      # electron-builder reach doSign(), which runs our ad-hoc hook (deep ad-hoc
      # sign via @electron/osx-sign + an explicit root-bundle re-seal).
      - name: Package desktop app (macOS ad-hoc)
        if: matrix.ebflag == '--mac' && steps.mac_secrets.outputs.has_secrets != 'true'
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
          MACOS_ADHOC_SIGN: "1"
          # Issue #808: electron-builder's isSignAllowed() bails out with
          # "Current build is a part of pull request, code signing will be
          # skipped" whenever GITHUB_BASE_REF is set (builder-util
          # `isPullRequest()`), so the pull-request dry run produced an unsigned
          # .app with no CodeResources and the smoke test failed. The security
          # warning attached to this flag is about *secret* certificates leaking
          # to fork builds; this step only runs when no signing secrets exist and
          # signs ad-hoc with identity `-`, so there is nothing to leak.
          CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST: "true"
          FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG: "1"
          DEBUG: electron-builder,electron-osx-sign*
          # Wall-clock ceiling for packaging including retries, derived from the
          # job's own clock rather than guessed. `timeout-minutes` reports the
          # kill it performs as **cancelled**, not failed, which is exactly the
          # false negative this issue exists to remove, so a retry that cannot
          # finish inside the cap must not be started.
          #
          # The number has to be derived because packaging does not start at a
          # fixed point: in run 95255998673 it began 28 min into the job (26 of
          # them in `cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml`) and finished 43.7 min into a 50-minute cap,
          # while run 30788311906 compiled for 33m21s before packaging at all.
          # With this deadline the wrapper sees ~936s left in the first case --
          # room for a retry after a healthy ~320s attempt, none after the 919s
          # stalled one -- and ~495s in the second, where there is no room for a
          # retry and it correctly declines to try.
          FORMAL_AI_MACOS_PACKAGE_DEADLINE_EPOCH: ${{ env.FORMAL_AI_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH }}
        run: bash scripts/package-macos-with-retry.sh ${{ matrix.ebflag }} --publish never -c.mac.notarize=false -c.mac.identity=- -c.mac.sign=./scripts/adhoc-sign-mac.cjs

      - name: Normalize desktop artifact names
        working-directory: desktop
        run: node scripts/normalize-artifacts.mjs

      - name: Smoke test macOS release artifacts
        if: matrix.ebflag == '--mac'
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          MACOS_BUILD_MODE: ${{ steps.mac_secrets.outputs.mode }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob

          VERSION="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          case "${{ matrix.label }}" in
            macos-x64) ARCH="x64" ;;
            macos-arm64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::Unexpected macOS matrix label: ${{ matrix.label }}"
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

          required_macos_artifacts=(
            "release/formal-ai-desktop-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.dmg"
            "release/formal-ai-desktop-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.zip"
          )
          for artifact in "${required_macos_artifacts[@]}"; do
            if [ ! -f "$artifact" ]; then
              echo "::error file=$artifact::Expected versioned macOS release artifact was not created."
              ls -la release || true
              exit 1
            fi
          done

          # An array, not a bare quoted word: `for x in "a"` reads as an attempt
          # to word-split and is flagged by shellcheck (SC2066). Behaviour is
          # unchanged -- exactly one DMG per matrix arch.
          dmgs=("release/formal-ai-desktop-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.dmg")
          for dmg in "${dmgs[@]}"; do
            echo "Mounting DMG: $dmg"
            mount_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
            installed_app="$RUNNER_TEMP/formal-ai Desktop.app"

            hdiutil attach "$dmg" -mountpoint "$mount_dir" -nobrowse -readonly
            mounted_app="$mount_dir/formal-ai Desktop.app"

            if [ ! -d "$mounted_app" ]; then
              echo "::error file=$dmg::Mounted DMG does not contain formal-ai Desktop.app."
              find "$mount_dir" -maxdepth 2 -print
              hdiutil detach "$mount_dir"
              exit 1
            fi

            rm -rf "$installed_app"
            ditto "$mounted_app" "$installed_app"
            hdiutil detach "$mount_dir"

            app_info="$installed_app/Contents/Info.plist"
            executable="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleExecutable' "$app_info")"
            bundle_id="$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :CFBundleIdentifier' "$app_info")"

            if [ "$bundle_id" != "ai.formal.desktop" ]; then
              echo "::error file=$dmg::Unexpected macOS app bundle identifier: $bundle_id"
              exit 1
            fi

            if [ ! -x "$installed_app/Contents/MacOS/$executable" ]; then
              echo "::error file=$dmg::Mounted app executable is missing or not executable."
              find "$installed_app/Contents" -maxdepth 3 -print
              exit 1
            fi

            if [ ! -f "$installed_app/Contents/_CodeSignature/CodeResources" ]; then
              echo "::error file=$dmg::Mounted app is missing its signed CodeResources envelope."
              find "$installed_app/Contents/_CodeSignature" -maxdepth 1 -print 2>/dev/null || true
              exit 1
            fi

            codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$installed_app"

            if [ "$MACOS_BUILD_MODE" = "signed" ]; then
              spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=4 "$installed_app"
              xcrun stapler validate "$installed_app"
            else
              codesign --display --verbose=2 "$installed_app" 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/formal-ai-macos-codesign.txt"
              if ! grep -Fq 'Signature=adhoc' "$RUNNER_TEMP/formal-ai-macos-codesign.txt"; then
                echo "::error file=$dmg::Expected ad-hoc macOS signature for no-Apple-account build."
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
          done

      # The macOS smoke test above is the only artifact verification this
      # workflow had, so the four Linux/Windows targets were uploaded to the
      # release with nothing checking that electron-builder actually produced
      # them under the expected names. A rename or a partial package silently
      # shipped. The deep checks are macOS-only by nature (hdiutil, codesign),
      # but existence and non-emptiness are checkable everywhere.
      - name: Smoke test Linux/Windows release artifacts
        if: matrix.ebflag != '--mac'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: desktop
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          VERSION="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          case "${{ matrix.label }}" in
            linux-x64|linux-arm64)
              ARCH="${{ matrix.label }}"; ARCH="${ARCH#linux-}"
              required=(
                "release/formal-ai-desktop-linux-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.AppImage"
                "release/formal-ai-desktop-linux-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.deb"
                "release/formal-ai-desktop-linux-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.tar.gz"
              )
              ;;
            windows-x64|windows-arm64)
              ARCH="${{ matrix.label }}"; ARCH="${ARCH#windows-}"
              required=(
                "release/formal-ai-desktop-windows-installer-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.exe"
                "release/formal-ai-desktop-windows-portable-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.exe"
              )
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::Unexpected matrix label for the Linux/Windows smoke test: ${{ matrix.label }}"
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

          failed=0
          for artifact in "${required[@]}"; do
            if [ ! -f "$artifact" ]; then
              echo "::error file=$artifact::Expected versioned release artifact was not created."
              failed=1
            elif [ ! -s "$artifact" ]; then
              echo "::error file=$artifact::Release artifact is empty."
              failed=1
            else
              echo "ok $artifact ($(wc -c < "$artifact") bytes)"
            fi
          done
          if [ "$failed" -ne 0 ]; then
            ls -la release || true
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Collect artifacts and checksums
        id: collect
        working-directory: desktop
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          files=()
          for f in release/formal-ai-desktop-*; do
            case "$f" in
              *.dmg|*.zip|*.exe|*.AppImage|*.deb|*.tar.gz|*.blockmap) files+=("$f") ;;
            esac
          done
          for f in release/latest.yml release/latest-mac.yml release/latest-linux.yml; do
            [ -f "$f" ] && files+=("$f")
          done
          if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "No desktop artifacts produced for ${{ matrix.label }}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          printf 'Artifacts:\n'; printf '  %s\n' "${files[@]}"
          # Standard `sha256sum`-format lines with bare filenames so the
          # in-browser verifier on the /download page can match by name.
          node -e '
            const fs = require("fs"); const cp = require("crypto"); const path = require("path");
            const dir = "release";
            const re = /^(formal-ai-desktop-.*\.(dmg|zip|exe|AppImage|deb|tar\.gz|blockmap)|latest(-mac|-linux)?\.yml)$/;
            const names = fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((n) => re.test(n)).sort();
            for (const n of names) {
              const hash = cp.createHash("sha256").update(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, n))).digest("hex");
              process.stdout.write(hash + "  " + n + "\n");
            }
          ' > "release/SHA256SUMS-${{ matrix.label }}.partial"
          cat "release/SHA256SUMS-${{ matrix.label }}.partial"

      # Attest before publishing, not after: uploading first left the assets
      # downloadable for the length of the attest step, and permanently so if
      # attest failed, with `gh attestation verify` unable to vouch for them.
      - name: Attest build provenance
        # Dry run: a pull request has nothing to attest and no release to
        # publish to. Everything above -- packaging, signing, smoke tests -- has
        # already run, which is what catches desktop regressions before merge.
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/attest@v4
        with:
          # The released v4 checksum parser splits with the runner's native EOL,
          # so it treats our intentionally portable LF manifest as one record on
          # Windows. Digest the artifacts directly; keep the checksum fragment
          # solely for the consolidated, user-facing SHA256SUMS.txt.
          subject-path: |
            desktop/release/formal-ai-desktop-*
            desktop/release/latest*.yml

      - name: Upload assets to release
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          files=()
          for f in release/formal-ai-desktop-*; do
            case "$f" in
              *.dmg|*.zip|*.exe|*.AppImage|*.deb|*.tar.gz|*.blockmap) files+=("$f") ;;
            esac
          done
          for f in release/latest.yml release/latest-mac.yml release/latest-linux.yml; do
            [ -f "$f" ] && files+=("$f")
          done
          gh release upload "$TAG" "${files[@]}" --repo "$REPO" --clobber

      - name: Upload checksum fragment
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: checksums-${{ matrix.label }}
          path: desktop/release/SHA256SUMS-${{ matrix.label }}.partial
          retention-days: 7

  # Issue #1181 (R1-R5): ship the `formal-ai` CLI binary itself as standalone
  # release archives, so `curl | tar xz` (or `cargo binstall formal-ai`, whose
  # [package.metadata.binstall] in rust/Cargo.toml points at these names) works
  # without a Rust toolchain and without building the desktop app. Five
  # targets, one per archive:
  #   formal-ai-cli-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz   (static, no glibc dependency)
  #   formal-ai-cli-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz  (static)
  #   formal-ai-cli-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
  #   formal-ai-cli-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
  #   formal-ai-cli-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip
  # Each archive holds `formal-ai-cli-<triple>/` with the binary, LICENSE and
  # README.md. Names are version-less because GitHub Releases namespaces assets
  # per tag; scripts/install.sh resolves the release by tag, so a stable name
  # keeps the download path (and binstall's pkg-url) independent of the version
  # string embedded everywhere else.
  cli:
    name: Build CLI ${{ matrix.label }}
    needs: [resolve, base]
    concurrency:
      group: desktop-release-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}-cli-${{ matrix.label }}
      queue: max
    # Same skipped-dependency handling as `build`; see the comment there.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || needs.resolve.outputs.should_build == 'true') }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # `capmin` mirrors `build`'s per-target job clock: the macos-15-intel
        # and windows runners have measured the slowest cold compiles of this
        # dependency graph (runs 30788311906, 30832897812), and this job
        # compiles the same crate the desktop legs do.
        include:
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,    target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, label: cli-linux-x64,   binext: "",   archive: tar.gz, capmin: 40 }
          - { os: ubuntu-24.04-arm, target: aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, label: cli-linux-arm64, binext: "",   archive: tar.gz, capmin: 40 }
          - { os: macos-15-intel,   target: x86_64-apple-darwin,        label: cli-macos-x64,   binext: "",   archive: tar.gz, capmin: 50 }
          - { os: macos-14,         target: aarch64-apple-darwin,        label: cli-macos-arm64, binext: "",   archive: tar.gz, capmin: 40 }
          - { os: windows-latest,   target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc,      label: cli-windows-x64, binext: ".exe", archive: zip,  capmin: 50 }
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.capmin }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Same ref/fetch-depth reasoning as `build`: PRs build the merge
          # preview below, releases build the resolved tag.
          ref: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.resolve.outputs.tag || '' }}
          fetch-depth: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '0' || '1' }}

      # Same reason as `build`: package the merge result, not a stale preview
      # (issue #812), and merge the same pinned commit as every other leg
      # (issue #1017).
      - name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          BASE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.base.outputs.commit }}
        run: bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      # The two Linux legs cross-compile to musl for a static binary with no
      # glibc dependency. The crate's dependency graph compiles C code
      # (tree-sitter grammars through meta-language, aws-lc-sys through
      # webrtc's rustls), so a bare `rustup target add` is not enough: this
      # action installs the musl GCC and sets CC/CFLAGS/CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE
      # for the target. Native legs (macOS both arches, Windows x64) need
      # nothing beyond the toolchain above.
      - name: Set up the musl cross toolchain
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: taiki-e/setup-cross-toolchain-action@v1
        with:
          target: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Cache Rust compiler outputs
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        uses: mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.11
        with:
          # Same response-file constraint as `build` (os error 206 on Windows).
          version: v0.16.0

      - name: Enable Rust compiler cache
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          echo "SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build formal-ai CLI binary (release, pinned lock)
        run: cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --target-dir target --release --bin formal-ai --locked --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Package the CLI archive
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          triple="${{ matrix.target }}"
          staging="formal-ai-cli-${triple}"
          mkdir "$staging"
          cp "target/${triple}/release/formal-ai${{ matrix.binext }}" "$staging/"
          cp LICENSE README.md "$staging/"
          case "${{ matrix.archive }}" in
            tar.gz) tar -czf "${staging}.tar.gz" "$staging" ;;
            # Windows: Compress-Archive, not `tar -a` — the bash `tar` on the
            # Windows runners may be GNU tar, which cannot write zip at all;
            # PowerShell's archiver is present on every Windows runner.
            zip) powershell -NoLogo -Command "Compress-Archive -Path '${staging}' -DestinationPath '${staging}.zip'" ;;
            *) echo "::error::Unexpected archive format: ${{ matrix.archive }}"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          ls -la "${staging}.${{ matrix.archive }}"

      # The one artifact verification this job has (mirroring the desktop
      # legs' smoke tests): extract the just-built archive and run the binary
      # from it. Every leg builds for its own host arch (musl included -- a
      # static musl binary executes on the glibc host), so each leg is the one
      # runner that can actually execute its own archive. A target that
      # compiles but cannot start (bad linker flags, a broken manifest, a
      # packaging mistake) fails here instead of in a user's shell.
      - name: Smoke test CLI archive
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          triple="${{ matrix.target }}"
          checkdir="smoke-${triple}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "tar.gz" ]; then
            mkdir "$checkdir"
            tar -xzf "formal-ai-cli-${triple}.tar.gz" -C "$checkdir"
          else
            # Expand-Archive needs the directory to exist first.
            mkdir "$checkdir"
            powershell -NoLogo -Command "Expand-Archive -Path 'formal-ai-cli-${triple}.zip' -DestinationPath '${checkdir}'"
          fi
          binary="${checkdir}/formal-ai-cli-${triple}/formal-ai${{ matrix.binext }}"
          [ -s "$binary" ] || { echo "::error::the archive did not contain the binary"; exit 1; }
          "$binary" --version
          [ -s "${checkdir}/formal-ai-cli-${triple}/LICENSE" ] || { echo "::error::the archive did not contain LICENSE"; exit 1; }
          [ -s "${checkdir}/formal-ai-cli-${triple}/README.md" ] || { echo "::error::the archive did not contain README.md"; exit 1; }

      # Same `sha256sum`-format line (bare filename) as the desktop build job
      # so the consolidated SHA256SUMS.txt covers the CLI archives too and
      # scripts/install.sh can verify its download against it by name.
      - name: Collect CLI checksum fragment
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # macOS runners ship `shasum`, not `sha256sum`; both print `hash  name`.
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null; then sum=(sha256sum); else sum=(shasum -a 256); fi
          "${sum[@]}" "formal-ai-cli-${{ matrix.target }}.${{ matrix.archive }}" \
            > "SHA256SUMS-${{ matrix.label }}.partial"
          cat "SHA256SUMS-${{ matrix.label }}.partial"

      # Attest before publishing; see the same step in the desktop build job.
      - name: Attest build provenance
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/attest@v4
        with:
          # The exact archive this leg produced (.tar.gz or .zip), not a glob:
          # a glob that matches nothing on a leg makes attest fail the job.
          subject-path: formal-ai-cli-${{ matrix.target }}.${{ matrix.archive }}

      - name: Upload CLI archive to release
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release upload "$TAG" "formal-ai-cli-${{ matrix.target }}.${{ matrix.archive }}" --repo "$REPO" --clobber

      - name: Upload checksum fragment
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: checksums-${{ matrix.label }}
          path: SHA256SUMS-${{ matrix.label }}.partial
          retention-days: 7

  vscode:
    name: Package VS Code extension (.vsix)
    needs: [resolve, base]
    concurrency:
      group: desktop-release-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}-vscode
      queue: max
    # Same skipped-dependency handling as `build`; see the comment there.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || needs.resolve.outputs.should_build == 'true') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # On pull requests there is no resolved tag: build the PR head, which
          # is the whole point of the dry run.
          ref: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.resolve.outputs.tag || '' }}
          # See the note in `build`: quoted so the number 0 is not read as falsy.
          fetch-depth: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '0' || '1' }}

      # Same reason as `build`: package the merge result, not a stale preview.
      - name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          # Issue #1017: same pinned commit the packaging legs merge, so the
          # .vsix and the installers cannot come from different source trees.
          BASE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.base.outputs.commit }}
        run: bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # Install the committed extension lock through the warning classifier so
      # this package job exercises the exact production and build-tool graph.
      - name: Install extension dependencies
        run: scripts/install-node-dependencies.sh vscode

      # Issue #1014: the source-only lint suite intentionally needs no install.
      # Exercise the real esbuild + Playwright graph here, after its locked
      # dependencies exist and before the same helper creates the VSIX.
      - name: Test extension production bundle
        working-directory: vscode
        run: npm run test:package

      - name: Package the .vsix
        id: package
        working-directory: vscode
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # `vscode:prepublish` (prepare-resources.mjs) syncs the extension
          # version from Cargo.toml and copies js + data/seed + desktop/lib
          # into the package, so the .vsix is fully self-contained and its
          # filename (formal-ai-vscode-<version>.vsix) matches the release
          # version the /download and /vscode pages resolve.
          npm run package
          # A glob, not `ls | head`: `ls` output is not safe to parse and its
          # exit status is swallowed here (shellcheck SC2012).
          shopt -s nullglob
          vsix_files=(formal-ai-vscode-*.vsix)
          vsix="${vsix_files[0]:-}"
          [ -n "$vsix" ] || { echo "::error::vsce package produced no .vsix" >&2; exit 1; }
          echo "vsix=$vsix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Packaged: $vsix"

      - name: Collect .vsix checksum fragment
        working-directory: vscode
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Same `sha256sum`-format line (bare filename) as the desktop build job
          # so the consolidated SHA256SUMS.txt covers the .vsix too, and both the
          # /download verifier and install.sh can match it by name.
          node -e '
            const fs = require("fs"); const cp = require("crypto");
            const n = fs.readdirSync(".").filter((f) => /^formal-ai-vscode-.*\.vsix$/.test(f)).sort()[0];
            if (!n) { process.exit(1); }
            const hash = cp.createHash("sha256").update(fs.readFileSync(n)).digest("hex");
            process.stdout.write(hash + "  " + n + "\n");
          ' > SHA256SUMS-vscode.partial
          cat SHA256SUMS-vscode.partial

      # Attest before publishing; see the same step in the desktop build job.
      - name: Attest build provenance
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/attest@v4
        with:
          subject-path: vscode/formal-ai-vscode-*.vsix

      - name: Upload .vsix to release
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        working-directory: vscode
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}
        run: gh release upload "$TAG" "${{ steps.package.outputs.vsix }}" --repo "$REPO" --clobber

      - name: Upload checksum fragment
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: checksums-vscode
          path: vscode/SHA256SUMS-vscode.partial
          retention-days: 7

  finalize:
    name: Publish SHA256SUMS.txt + provenance
    needs: [resolve, build, cli, vscode]
    concurrency:
      group: formal-ai-repository-writes
      queue: max
    # !cancelled(), not always(): a partial matrix (one arch failing under
    # fail-fast:false) must still publish checksums for the arches that did
    # build, but a *cancelled* run must not. The upload below uses
    # `gh release upload --clobber`, so under always() a run cancelled part-way
    # -- by the concurrency group superseding it, or by hand -- would overwrite a
    # complete SHA256SUMS.txt from an earlier successful run with a manifest
    # covering whichever one or two arches happened to finish (issue #812).
    # Never on pull requests: there is no release to publish checksums to.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.resolve.outputs.should_build == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Download checksum fragments
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        env:
          # v8's bundled unzip dependency still calls Buffer(); suppress only
          # that reviewed upstream diagnostic, never all Node warnings:
          # https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/issues/484
          NODE_OPTIONS: --disable-warning=DEP0005
        with:
          pattern: checksums-*
          path: fragments
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Build consolidated SHA256SUMS.txt and BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt
        id: manifest
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          parts=(fragments/*.partial)
          if [ ${#parts[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "No checksum fragments were produced; nothing to finalize." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          # Deterministic order: concatenate fragments, sort by filename (field 2).
          cat "${parts[@]}" | sort -k2 > SHA256SUMS.txt
          echo "=== SHA256SUMS.txt ==="
          cat SHA256SUMS.txt
          commit="$(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$REPO" --json targetCommitish --jq .targetCommitish || echo unknown)"

          # Report the builders that actually produced a fragment. Hardcoding the
          # full matrix here claimed builds that never happened whenever an arch
          # failed under fail-fast: false.
          declare -A builder_of=(
            [linux-x64]="ubuntu-latest"
            [linux-arm64]="ubuntu-24.04-arm"
            [macos-x64]="macos-15-intel"
            [macos-arm64]="macos-14"
            [windows-x64]="windows-latest"
            [windows-arm64]="windows-11-arm"
            [cli-linux-x64]="ubuntu-latest"
            [cli-linux-arm64]="ubuntu-24.04-arm"
            [cli-macos-x64]="macos-15-intel"
            [cli-macos-arm64]="macos-14"
            [cli-windows-x64]="windows-latest"
            [vscode]="ubuntu-latest"
          )
          built=()
          missing=()
          for label in linux-x64 linux-arm64 macos-x64 macos-arm64 windows-x64 windows-arm64 cli-linux-x64 cli-linux-arm64 cli-macos-x64 cli-macos-arm64 cli-windows-x64 vscode; do
            if [ -f "fragments/SHA256SUMS-${label}.partial" ]; then
              built+=("${builder_of[$label]} (${label})")
            else
              missing+=("$label")
            fi
          done

          {
            echo "formal-ai Desktop build provenance"
            echo "=================================="
            echo "Repository : $REPO"
            echo "Release tag: $TAG"
            echo "Commitish  : $commit"
            echo "Workflow   : Desktop Release"
            echo "Run        : $RUN_URL"
            printf 'Builders   : %s\n' "${built[0]}"
            printf '             %s\n' "${built[@]:1}"
            if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "INCOMPLETE : no artifacts from: ${missing[*]}"
              echo "             This release is missing those targets; the checksums"
              echo "             below cover only the builders listed above."
            fi
            echo "Signing    : macOS artifacts are ad-hoc signed (no Apple Developer ID)."
            echo "Attestation: SLSA build provenance attached via actions/attest."
            echo "             Verify with: gh attestation verify <file> --repo $REPO"
            echo ""
            # Deliberately not "authoritative": when `missing` is non-empty this
            # manifest covers only part of the release, and calling it
            # authoritative is exactly the false positive we are fixing.
            echo "SHA-256 checksums of the artifacts listed above (SHA256SUMS.txt is the machine-readable copy):"
            echo ""
            cat SHA256SUMS.txt
          } > BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt
          echo "=== BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt ==="
          cat BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt

          # Still upload what we have (a partial manifest beats none), but never
          # report success for it: a green run here means "all desktop assets
          # shipped", and callers rely on that.
          if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "incomplete=${missing[*]}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Upload SHA256SUMS.txt and BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt to release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release upload "$TAG" SHA256SUMS.txt BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt --repo "$REPO" --clobber

      # Runs after the upload so the partial manifest is still published for
      # debugging, but the run ends red.
      - name: Fail if any target produced no artifacts
        if: ${{ steps.manifest.outputs.incomplete != '' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error title=Incomplete desktop release::No artifacts from: ${{ steps.manifest.outputs.incomplete }}. SHA256SUMS.txt was published but covers only the targets that built."
          exit 1
